events.title: Diocletian, Galerius and Maximian confer at Carnuntum
events.description: With the former emperors Diocletian and Maximian present, Galerius appointed Licinius as Augustus in place of Severus, killed by Maxentius, and Maximian was ordered to step down for good. The meeting aimed to end the civil wars of the Tetrarchy.

events.title: Pope Innocent III opens the Fourth Lateran Council
events.description: The largest church council of the Middle Ages met in Rome under Innocent III. It defined transubstantiation, required annual confession and ordered Jews and Muslims to wear distinguishing dress.
events.html: The largest church council of the Middle Ages met in Rome under Innocent III. It defined transubstantiation, required annual confession and ordered Jews and Muslims to wear distinguishing dress.

events.title: The Council of Constance elects Martin V, ending the Western Schism
events.description: The Council of Constance elected Oddone Colonna as Pope Martin V, having deposed or accepted the resignation of the remaining papal claimants. His election ended the Western Schism of 1378, in which bishops in Rome and Avignon had both claimed to be pope.

events.title: Louis XII and Ferdinand II secretly agree to divide Naples
events.description: In the secret Treaty of Granada, Louis XII of France and Ferdinand II of Aragon agreed to partition the Kingdom of Naples. Disputes between France and the Hispanic kingdoms led to the treaty's collapse in 1503.

events.title: Riots break out in Lhasa after the murder of Tibet's expected regent
events.description: An uprising began in Lhasa after two Qing ambans assassinated Gyurme Namgyal, the expected new regent of Tibet; both ambans were killed, with 51 Qing soldiers and 77 Chinese citizens. A year later the Qing executed the rebel leader Lobsang Trashi.

events.title: British and Iroquois forces attack Cherry Valley, New York
events.description: A mixed force of Loyalists, British soldiers, Senecas and Mohawks attacked the fort and town of Cherry Valley in central New York, whose defenders were unprepared despite warnings. The attackers killed 14 soldiers and 30 civilians.

events.title: Nat Turner is hanged in Virginia
events.description: Nat Turner was executed at Jerusalem, Virginia, for leading the August revolt in which about 55 to 60 white people were killed. Reprisals killed many more Black people, and southern states tightened slave codes.

events.title: The armistice ends fighting on the Western Front
events.description: Signed at 5 a.m. in a railway carriage in the forest of Compiègne, the armistice between Germany and the Allies took effect at 11 o'clock. The day is marked as Armistice or Remembrance Day.

events.title: The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is dedicated at Arlington
events.description: President Harding presided as an unidentified American soldier from the Western Front was buried at Arlington National Cemetery. A year earlier, Britain and France had interred their own unknown warriors.
events.html: President Harding presided as an unidentified American soldier from the Western Front was buried at Arlington National Cemetery. A year earlier, Britain and France had interred their own unknown warriors.

events.title: Rhodesia declares independence from Britain
events.description: Ian Smith's white minority government issued a Unilateral Declaration of Independence to avoid majority rule. Britain and the UN imposed sanctions, and after a long guerrilla war Zimbabwe became independent in 1980.

intl.name: Remembrance Day
intl.description: Observed each year at the eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month — the moment the Armistice ending the First World War took effect in 1918 — Remembrance Day honours the sacrifice of military personnel who have died in all wars since.

song: Anglo-American popular music and the peace movement of the early 1970s
A 1971 song by John Lennon and Yoko Ono that asks listeners to picture a world living together in peace.
